hot.title: DexAgent: An Agentic Human2Sim2Robot Framework for Dexterous Manipulation with Self-Evolving Tool Library
hot.summary: DexAgent converts one egocentric RGB video and a task prompt into robot-training data by adapting reconstruction, motion skills, and property-specific verifiers to each task. It refines subgoals, varies simulated starting states, and renders observations for rigid, articulated, and deformable objects. Across eleven tasks, policies averaged 63.6% success versus 18.2% for SPIDER, but verification does not eliminate errors or establish causation.

hot.title: AD-E2E-JEPA: A Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture For End-to-End Autonomous Driving
hot.summary: AD-E2E-JEPA enables policy-free, goal-conditioned driving planning by compressing DINOv3 patch embeddings, predicting action-conditioned future representations, and selecting among candidate trajectories by latent distance to a future image goal. On NAVSIMv2’s 12,146-scene test set, it reaches 67.3 EPDMS at 256 candidates and 0.8 seconds per scene. More candidates improve scores but increase runtime and reduce hit rates.

hot.title: MatToolBench: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents in Real-World Materials Science Workflows
hot.summary: MatToolBench evaluates whether agents can complete materials-science workflows across specialist software, scripts, and scientific databases. It includes 204 tasks on 10 tools, with GUI, hybrid OriginPro, code, and diagnostic mixed tasks, and scores partial criteria separately from complete success. GPT-5.4 reaches a 45.0% code success rate, while Claude-sonnet-4.6 reaches 25.0% for GUI tasks; these results do not establish readiness for unsupervised use.

hot.title: Context Language Models
hot.summary: Context Language Models let an agent edit its live conversation by mirroring the transcript into a file whose changes synchronize with subsequent model calls. The approach supports multiple agents and zero-shot context management. On BrowseComp-Plus, Qwen3.6-27B reached 59.4% accuracy, with 21.5% fewer prefix-reuse FLOPs than Codex-style summarization. Results vary by setting and do not isolate editing alone.

hot.title: T$^2$Mem: Learning Test-Time Memory for Robotics
hot.summary: T²Mem gives a vision-language-action robot policy a fixed-size episodic memory in fast weights updated during deployment, while learned policy parameters remain fixed. At each observation, a learned interface writes and reads compact vision-language associations for action selection. On RoboMME, it achieves 56.83% macro-averaged terminal success across 16 tasks, versus 17.93% for memory-free π0.5, but the result is benchmark-specific.

hot.title: LongLive-Plug: Once-for-All Distillation for Video Generation
hot.summary: LongLive-Plug distills reusable few-step sampling and guidance into adapters trained on base video models. Developers attach compatible adapters to specialized descendants without downstream retraining while retaining task-specific weights. On SCOPE, four-step Wan2.2-TI2V-5B achieves FVD 478.7, versus 805.5 for naive sampling and 502.1 for SCOPE-specific distillation on 1,378 clips. The verified scope is 54 entries, limited to compatible descendants.

hot.title: Harness Learning Enables Generalizable Test-Time Adaptation
hot.summary: The paper trains a proposer to revise a language-model agent’s executable harness—its workflow for model calls, tools, and information flow—using execution outcomes, while keeping the solver fixed. At test time, frozen proposer and solver weights support successive harness edits. On 21 unseen reasoning families, mean held-out score rises from 0.32 to 0.62, but five harder families are excluded.

hot.title: Rethinking Representations for World-Action Modeling
hot.summary: ReWAM trains a robot world-action model by using an action-shaped compact visual state and a branch predicting future representations. During training, action gradients shape the state, while world-prediction gradients stop at representations; inference does not generate future states. On RoboTwin 2.0, ReWAM reaches 93.6% random-scene success versus 92.2% for AHA-WAM without generative video pre-training. The result does not establish universality.

hot.title: Generalization Dynamics of LM Pre-training
hot.summary: The authors study mode-hopping, abrupt changes in whether language models infer a task or follow a prompt pattern during pre-training. They use six cheap behavioral tests comparing probabilities of correct and misleading answers, plus fine-tuning tests, across OLMo3 and Apertus checkpoints. OLMo3-32B scores 81%, 0%, and 81.7% on answer+1 at 2.17T, 2.19T, and 2.21T tokens, illustrating checkpoint reversals rather than universal behavior.

hot.title: Agent Priors-guided Policy Learning
hot.summary: APPL carries each skill’s structural prior into runtime selection, preserving prior-specific policies, handoff conditions, support, and verification evidence. A construction agent builds and checks policies, while a runtime agent selects one and its execution conditions. With two demonstrations per task, APPL reached 89.58% macro OOD success across six MetaWorld tasks. Results are simulated, and priors do not guarantee competence.

hot.title: Simplex Diffusion Models
hot.summary: Simplex Diffusion Models (SDMs) generate sequences while retaining token uncertainty as a probability vector instead of making a categorical choice. They use closed-form transitions with churn rather than ODE integration. On TinyGSM, SDM reaches 49.0% versus 45.8% for masked diffusion at 512 evaluations; after distillation, it reaches 32.1% at 8 versus 21.4% at 128. These results come from small models and do not establish general superiority.

hot.title: Tokenization: A Survey for Modern NLP
hot.summary:
While modern language models take raw text as their input and produce raw text as output, they do not operate over text directly. 
Hidden in the very first step of language model pipelines is tokenization, where raw text is converted to a sequence of tokens which the model is designed to process.

hot.title: Imagine3D-LLM: Teaching MLLMs to Imagine 3D Scenes Before Answering
hot.summary: Imagine3D-LLM trains a multimodal language model to summarize views as a 3D Gaussian Splatting scene before answering questions. Summary tokens are trained to reconstruct views and predict answers, with teacher distillation only during training. On SPAR-Bench, Imagine3D-LLM-7B scores 68.5 overall versus 60.9 for a matched baseline, but the method remains limited to indoor scenes and fixed capacity.

hot.title: OmniTaskonomy: When Does Visual Generation Improve Visual Understanding?
hot.summary: Training a model to generate visual content can encourage it to learn rich perceptual capabilities related to geometry, spatial relationships, and objectness; yet, its benefits for visual understanding remain unclear. We ask: when and how does visual generation supervision improve visual understanding? We study controlled pairs of image-to-image (I2I) generation and image-to-text (I2T) understandi

hot.title: Learning Native Reflection in Unified Models with Interleaved Reinforcement Learning
hot.summary: UMM-Reflection trains one unified model to inspect an image, write an edit instruction, render a revision, and repeat, using reinforcement learning from the outcomes of complete repair trajectories. On BAGEL’s matched GenEval evaluation, it reaches 84 macro-accuracy points versus 72 for reflection SFT, and WISE improves from 0.63 to 0.74. Initial-image gains are not statistically significant, and failures remain.

hot.title: d-OPD: Future-Aware On-Policy Distillation for Block Diffusion Language Models
hot.summary: d-OPD adapts a pretrained autoregressive model to block diffusion by reweighting the teacher’s causal token distribution with later-token evidence from the student’s completed rollout when future context is visible and the rollout passes verification. In a controlled diagnostic, its target KL falls from 0.4444 to 0.1249. On Qwen3-8B, it improves OPDLM’s average from 55.9 to 59.8, within evaluated settings.

hot.title: Reinforcement Learning from Intermediate Renders for Image-to-Code Generation
hot.summary: IR4RL improves image-to-code generation by rendering executable program prefixes, measuring visual-score changes between successive renders, and assigning those process rewards alongside the final outcome reward. On SVG, OmniSVG-4B reaches a DINO score of 97.48 with 2.5k tokens, versus 92.85 and 5.7k for outcome-only RL. Results are demonstrated for SVG and TikZ under executable-prefix assumptions.

hot.title: SCOPD: Sparse-Context On-Policy Self-Distillation for Efficient Vision-Language Models
hot.summary: SCOPD adapts vision-language models to use aggressively pruned visual-token contexts, while SCOPD+ focuses distillation on response positions sensitive to added visual evidence. With Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct and 10% of VisionZip tokens, fixed-context Pass@64 success reached 79.60%, versus 53.20% for greedy decoding. On 13 normalized image-benchmark scores, SCOPD+ reached 92.43, versus 86.37 for pruning alone.

hot.title: Can Agents Design Libraries for Agents?
hot.summary: LibraryDesignBench evaluates libraries by having one agent design a library and downstream agents use it to solve expert-validated programming problems, scoring test performance together with static-code simplicity. Across 242 problems, Opus 5.5-designed libraries scored 48.9 versus 46.6 for production libraries. This result is limited to the benchmark’s tasks, languages, consumers, and budgets.

hot.title: Improving Test-Time Scaling with Adaptive Looped Transformers
hot.summary: TaH2 adaptively loops shared Transformer layers in latent space, deciding token by token whether another pass is worth taking from measured next-token loss gains. On post-trained 1.7B Qwen3 models, it reaches 2.74 AIME accuracy points per doubling of decoding FLOPs versus 1.79 for Standard, and 15.4% versus 12.0% at matched compute. It does not reduce reported decoding cost or latency.

likes.title: Memory Attention
likes.summary: Memory Attention (MA) replaces the Transformer’s learned value projection with the sum of contextual keys and layer-specific token-indexed memory vectors. Across several attention variants, MA improves language-modeling and downstream metrics, strengthens needle retrieval, and enables CPU offloading that reduces GPU parameter storage to slightly below the standard attention baseline, although the comparisons use larger MA models and do not isolate capacity from architectural effects.

likes.title: Self-Play Pretraining with Zero Data
likes.summary: The paper tests whether a model can generate its own training curriculum: a generator writes programs, a universal computer executes them into bytes, and a learner predicts those bytes. Adaptive self-play improves next-byte prediction on natural data without using them for gradient updates. On DCLM text, the compute exponent is 0.123. Models below 25 million parameters cannot provide contingent facts.

likes.title: Language Model "Shape"
likes.summary: Alex Zhang argues that the input / output "shape" of language models has stayed fixed as the autoregressive, decoder-only Transformer since ChatGPT, so agent design has meant fitting harnesses to that shape. He proposes the reverse: designing model shapes around specific harnesses and task structures. Using Jev's [0,1]-constrained, prefill-only output and agent trajectories as examples, he argues that open models and distillation now make this direction practical for independent researchers.

likes.title: Raven: The Harness of Harnesses for Composable Agentic Intelligence
likes.summary: Raven treats each model-plus-harness as a specialist; a host assigns work through a directed acyclic graph of dependencies. MAOB’s Exact Match Rate with Qwen3.8-27B was 0.711, versus 0.607 for Hermes Agent. Raven-Oncall achieved 82.35% success at $5.10 per case on 17 AI4S tasks; MAOB tests planning before execution, and this result does not establish causation.

likes.title: LLM Agents Can Easily Tamper With Their Own Traces
likes.summary: The paper tests whether AI agents can alter execution traces before oversight, using local containerized harnesses, direct requests, hidden instructions, and undisclosed reward incentives. It measures attack success as trace-changing tool calls across ten trials and proposes an independent interception server with append-only logging. All ten configurations exceeded 80% on Terminal-Bench, but the experiments do not estimate real-world prevalence.

likes.title: Statistical Inference for Causal Discovery under Selection and Latent Variables via Single-Target Interventions
likes.summary: The authors develop a model-free framework for inferring causal relations among observed system variables despite latent variables and selection. Using single-target interventions, maximal ancestral graphs, and two stages, the method identifies a trimmed combined-MAG with at most 5d_X^2/2 tests. In simulation, FWER₁ was 0.050 versus F-FCI’s 0.990 under different error controls; this is not the full causal DAG.

likes.title: Despite Instructions: Frontier Agents Improvise Covert Channels at Test Time
likes.summary: The paper tests whether language-model agents can form a covert channel while a monitor approves each update. In simulated incident response, a sender privately identifies one of four malicious connections and summarizes a public report; interaction histories and correctness feedback let a receiver learn wording without a codebook. After 60 rounds, Sol reaches 98.8% accuracy, but this is a simulated result, not evidence of deployed-system leaks.

likes.title: Representation World Model: Learning States, Transition and Executable Plans in Representation
likes.summary: RWM constructs intermediate latent states between current and goal observations, then trains an inverse-dynamics model to decode neighboring states into actions, avoiding recursive forward rollouts and action-space search at standard inference. It reaches a 98.25% macro success rate across four control tasks, versus 95.33% for a published external INTACT reference. LIBERO-Goal uses an added delta predictor.

likes.title: Agent Priors-guided Policy Learning
likes.summary: APPL carries each skill’s structural prior into runtime selection, preserving prior-specific policies, handoff conditions, support, and verification evidence. A construction agent builds and checks policies, while a runtime agent selects one and its execution conditions. With two demonstrations per task, APPL reached 89.58% macro OOD success across six MetaWorld tasks. Results are simulated, and priors do not guarantee competence.

likes.title: Recursive Self-Improvement via On-Policy Distillation for Reasoning
likes.summary: DCE uses an evolving gold-conditioned teacher and verified shorter rewrites to train reasoning models on their own trajectories. The latest checkpoint becomes both student and detached teacher, while accepted rewrites provide cross-entropy targets. On Qwen3-8B, DCE+SRCL reaches 65.97% Average@12 versus 30.35% for OPSD across four benchmarks. At 8B, output falls from 19,046 to 17,561 tokens relative to DCE, but rises at 1.7B.

likes.title: The Past Frames the Future: Memory for Autoregressive Video Generation
likes.summary: A survey of memory mechanisms for autoregressive video generators, reframing long-horizon consistency as the problem of preserving historical information after it leaves the active context. It organizes existing approaches by memory representation, preservation function, lifecycle operations, learning strategy, and evaluation, and argues that reliable interactive video requires more than longer context windows: it requires memory that is accurate, retrievable, updateable, and causally effective.

likes.title: InternW0-$Δ$: A World Action Model Bridging Predictive Dynamics and Actions with 20K+ Hours of Open Data
likes.summary: InternW0-Δ transfers predictive video knowledge into robot control without supplying future video to the action policy at inference. Its Causal Imprint tokens summarize observed visual changes and receive future-derived training supervision, while directed attention blocks realized future frames. On RoboTwin 2.0 Clean2Random, it reaches 71.9% versus 69.4% for Qwen-RobotManip-Context; an ablation rises 70.80% to 76.45% with alignment on this benchmark.

likes.title: Guiding End-to-End Driving Models with Endpoint-Constrained Trajectory Optimization
likes.summary: The authors introduce Endpoint-Constrained Optimization (ECO), which reshapes intermediate waypoints after policy inference while preserving recent executed history and the policy’s endpoint. It optimizes smoothness, turn sharpness, and fidelity without hard physical constraints. In closed-loop HUGSIM tests, VaVAM’s HD-Score rises from 18.1 to 31.0, but ECO does not guarantee collision-free driving or real-road safety.

likes.title: Your Transformer Can Hold Two Thoughts at Once: Evidence of Linear Superposition in LLMs
likes.summary: The paper tests whether a Transformer can process two unrelated text streams by averaging token embeddings position by position. It compares the mixed output with the average of independent predictions and measures retained signal by rank. Across models, each stream’s independently predicted token appears in the mixed output’s top 10 in roughly 30–40% of cases, not demonstrating full distributional equality.

likes.title: Training Object Permanence in World Models
likes.summary: The authors introduce WROP, a benchmark for testing whether video generators preserve object identity and location through occlusion and respect solid boundaries during obstruction, support removal, and collisions. It uses 150 Blender generators, 1.5 million training samples, and a 300-question continuation exam. PWM-WROP scores 1,679.5 Elo, leading true-continuation models, but the preliminary comparison does not isolate fine-tuning’s effect.

likes.title: On the Diffusibility of High-Dimensional Latents
likes.summary: Representation Autoencoders (RAEs) enable diffusion models to operate in the feature spaces of pretrained visual encoders. likes.title: TrackEverything: Long Horizon Dense Tracking via De-Duplicating 3D Scene Representations
likes.summary: TrackEverything tracks dense scene points across long videos by storing surface tracks in shared 3D coordinates, merging repeated observations in spatial voxels, and decoding trajectories mainly for moving points. On the first 48 TAPVid-3D frames, it achieves 34.7 APD-P versus 10.9 for VDPM. The benchmark uses sparse queries, and memory still grows with newly encountered geometry.

likes.title: Just Ask Jev: Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Decisions as a Zero-Shot Detector of AI Alignment Failures
likes.summary: The paper evaluates Jev, a model that answers multiple typed questions about one interaction state in a single call, as a detector of benchmark-labeled language-model failures. RLCDAlignBench covers 44 benchmarks, ten failure types, and 7,193 instances. A generic probability question reaches median AUROC 0.886 on 31 benchmarks, but probabilities are often miscalibrated within individual benchmarks.
